summary: A seat's delivery, read and close of graph mail are recorded on its own host as local marks instead of lifecycle claims, once every member reads them (db break-up step 4b, the writers)

replay.detail: Once marks are on, this member writes no message.staged, message.delivered, message.read or message.closed claim for a seat its own declarations place on it; it records a local mark instead (local_message_marks, and local_message_staged for a staging), which never replicates. Lifecycle claims already written keep counting, and readers take the further of a message's claims and marks. Persons, seats on other hosts, acted-for retired seats, delegated writes and native Claude-channel reads still write claims.

schema.detail: New member-local tables local_message_staged and local_message_mark_events, with their triggers; no change to any replicated table. Builds that read local_message_marks ignore both.

rules.detail: Marks are on only while every other current member advertises seat_freshness_reads=1, read from each member's own newest daemon.started at its incarnation; ambiguous membership counts as not ready, and a member alone switches at once. The daemon decides it at startup and every minute, so a member that joins without the feature turns marks off within a minute and writers return to claims. Every 4b-2 build advertises message_offsets=1, so other members ask it on the seat-freshness relay how far its seats got.

compatibility.detail: A member on a release without seat_freshness_reads (v0.3.24 and earlier) keeps every other member writing claims, so it reads lifecycle as before. Members with it read a marks-recording host's seats through the relay, and show unknown, never sent, when that host does not answer. Lifecycle requests (POST /v1/mailbox/receipts, POST /v1/messages/{id}/claims, cleanup, handoff acknowledgement) keep their request shapes; for a hosted seat they answer the mark's offset-receipt, whose store_index is 0.

downtime.detail: No migration: the new tables are created empty, and marks start with the next lifecycle write once the barrier holds.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to a release that reads message marks and advertises seat_freshness_reads (the first is expected to be v0.3.25) is safe: it reads the marks, redelivers nothing, and writes claims again from then on. Rolling back to v0.3.24 or earlier after marks were on shows mail delivered since then as undelivered, and its unread mail is redelivered once; a staging recorded as a mark is in flight again. Version 4 backups with marks restore on any release that reads them; stagings are not backed up.
